title: The close-out role cannot produce its own deliverable: the boundary forbids .tick/
description:
From the ticks pwp run, 2026-09-15. The close-out worker said it plainly in its own report:

  'The closeout cannot write .tick/ (run boundary), so the two learnings below live only in this report.'

The close-out role's deliverable IS the epic retro and .tick/learnings.md. The executor's boundary check forbids a worker from writing .tick/ — correct for an implement-tick worker, because the tracker is the RUN's to write and a worker editing tick state would race the reconciler. Applied to the closeout role it makes the job impossible.

Consequence observed: attempts 11, 12 and 13 each did the retro thinking, could commit none of it, and answered 'failed (no-commits)'. Each filed its conclusions as findings instead, which then blocked the tick on finding_untriaged, which stopped the run. Three dispatches, roughly 40 minutes of worker time, and the deliverable was carried out by hand by the operator in the end.

This is not a worker failure and no amount of prompt tuning fixes it. A role whose output is forbidden by the boundary it runs under is a design fault.

Options to weigh:
- Make the boundary ROLE-AWARE: closeout may write .tick/learnings.md and the retro path, nothing else under .tick/. Narrowest change, keeps tick STATE the run's alone.
- Have the RUN write the retro from the closeout's report, the way it already publishes notes and closes ticks from a worker's answer. Keeps the boundary absolute; moves the write to the writer that owns .tick/.
- Give closeout a distinct write channel outside the attempt branch that the run folds in.

Whichever is chosen, the boundary's refusal must name the role and say where the output should go, so a worker hitting it is not left inventing a workaround.

Acceptance: a closeout attempt commits the epic's retro and its learnings entries, the run integrates them, and an implement-tick attempt writing the same paths is still refused.
notes:
2026-09-15 08:30 - The finding 6a3af0d8 (checkpoint leaves gms at 'integrated' while the tracker says closed) was promoted here by mistake during triage. It is a separate defect from this tick's boundary contradiction, and its real home is tick 48q. Nothing about the checkpoint divergence should be worked here.
2026-09-15 09:17 - ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED, and it is smaller and worse than this tick's description says.

The description claims the boundary FORBIDS the closeout writing .tick/, making the role structurally impossible. That is wrong. internal/exec/subprocess/report.go has always exempted three paths:

    .tick/config.md
    .tick/runners.toml
    .tick/learnings.md

OutsideBoundary lets all three through. The closeout could have committed its learnings the whole time.

What actually happened: the PROMPT and the CHECK disagreed. The prompt said, flatly:

    - Do not run `tk`, and do not write under .tick/ or .ticfac/.

with no mention of the exemptions, while the same prompt's role section instructs the closeout to 'compact what was LEARNED into the repository's learnings' — a file under .tick/. Two contradictory instructions in one prompt. The worker obeyed the prohibition, correctly reported that it could not do its job, and filed its analysis as findings instead. Five attempts, each blind to the last (tick 35h), each surfacing a different subset.

So this was never a design fault in the boundary. It was drift between the rule and the telling of the rule, and it cost an entire closeout.

FIXED:
- ExemptFromBoundary() exported from internal/exec/subprocess/report.go as the single source.
- Both prompts (subprocess and herdr) now render the exemptions from that source, in the Boundaries section, as an explicit EXCEPT line.
- Three tests: the exempt list agrees with OutsideBoundary; every exemption sits inside a protected prefix (so a dead entry cannot pad the permission list); and the RENDERED prompt's Boundaries section names every exemption. The third is the one that would have caught this, and it is scoped to the Boundaries section deliberately — a whole-prompt Contains passes trivially, because .tick/learnings.md already appears earlier as a file to READ, which is precisely how the contradiction hid.

Verified by reverting the prompt change with the accessor in place: the rendered-prompt test fails naming all three paths, and passes with the fix.

STILL OPEN under this tick: nothing about the retro FILE. The closeout prompt asks for learnings, not a RETRO.md, and learnings.md is writable. If a retro file is ever wanted in a target repo, note that ticks' .tick/.gitignore ignores logs/, so ticfac's own .tick/logs/herd/<epic>/RETRO.md convention would be untracked there.
acceptance_criteria: A closeout attempt can commit the epic retro and .tick/learnings.md entries and the run integrates them; an implement-tick attempt writing any .tick/ path is still refused; the refusal message names the role and the permitted destination
